newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela shows Mrs Clinton his cell.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela shows Mrs Clinton his cell.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela showed U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton and her daughter Chelsea his tiny prison cell on Robben Island where he spent most of his 27 years in jail for opposing apartheid.
Mandela was imprisoned for 18 years on the island, overlooking the city of Cape Town, as part of a life sentence imposed by the apartheid government for his attempts to overthrow it by force.
"Would you like to come and join us," Mandela told reporters peeking through the window of the small cell.
Mrs Clinton, on the last day of her visit to South Africa, watched quietly as the 79-year-old Mandela showed her the yellow-painted cell, furnished with a table and a single bed.
He felt the mattress and told the Clintons the bed he had slept on had been bigger and he had put a plank under the mattress to ease in his back pain.
He showed them other parts of the prison and other cells where he had stayed and pointed to a wooden door saying: "When I was in this cell I acted usually as a spokesman for the prisoners".
Mandela said he was later moved to another cell at the end of the hall out of the way because other prisoners had relied on him to speak on their behalf.
As he and his visitors left the cell in the maximum security Block B, set aside for political prisoners, Mandela put his arm around Chelsea's shoulder.
He then led his visitors to the exercise courtyard and told Mrs Clinton pointing to a place alongside a wall: "I had a garden there."
A U.S. official on the tour said later Mandela's political manuscripts had been buried in the garden to hide them from guards.
Mrs Clinton toured other parts of the prison and drove down to the quarry where Mandela and his fellow prisoners had worked breaking rocks.
Ahmed Kathrada, a former prisoner on the island and now an adviser in Mandela's government, said although the work in the quarry had been debilitating prisoners had liked to be outdoors.
"Instead of being locked up in our cells the whole day we preferred to come out in spite of the hard work, but you get used to hard work, you don't get so used to loneliness in your cell," he said.

Asked her impression of the prison island Mrs Clinton said: "It's an extraordinary chance to be here and to be in his cell with him and come to this quarry and think about all those years that were spent here."
At the end of the tour U.S. comedian Bill Cosby appeared from a building.
Asked what he was doing on the island Cosby joked: "I don't want to go to jail anymore".
He is the star of a fund-raising dinner on the island on Thursday evening which will be attended by Mandela, Mrs Clinton and visiting U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan.
